message: The study contract is locked for planner handoff. Use the 25 June to 30 June window, keep the 30 June 11:00 PM cutoff hard, and preserve the time blocks and subject priorities shown below.

planning_notes: This intake is intentionally current-date and planner-ready.
Respect the hard deadline on 30 June at 11:00 PM local time.
The planner must not overlap user commitments or fresh calendar blockers.
Calendar-owned midday blockers dominate 25, 26, 29, and 30 June, so prefer morning and post-7 PM study windows on those days.
Treat daily_study_hours as already negotiated realistic study capacity, not as raw free time.
Use Mathematics and Science earlier in the window while the student is fresher; keep lighter Social Science recap later.
Use remaining_subtopics aggressively for sequencing because they reflect actual weak or pending work.
Avoid stacking two heavy numerical or formula-dense blocks back-to-back without a recall or concept buffer.
Keep the final day light and confidence-preserving.
If feasibility tightens, reduce Resources and Development depth before cutting core Mathematics or Science work.

study_items.subject: Mathematics
study_items.reason: Primary Maths repair item because formula recall is still shaky and mixed application questions are leaking marks.
planning_notes: Do this early in the window.
Mix formula recall with cone-cylinder-frustum application sets.
End with mixed word problems rather than only direct formula substitution.

planning_notes: Keep this practice-first.

Good candidate for a medium-energy slot.

study_items.subject: Science

planning_notes: Use labelled-diagram recall and oral self-explanation.
Break the chapter into nervous system, plant movement, and hormones.
Do not keep this too late at night because retention quality drops.

study_items.subject: Science

planning_notes: Pair numericals with sign-convention correction.

study_items.subject: Social Science
study_items.reason: Important theory chapter, but the learner mainly needs timeline, source, and map-linked recall rather than long reading.
planning_notes: Keep it recap-heavy and writing-light.
Use one timeline pass and one source recall pass.
Best suited to lower-energy evening or post-Maths recovery slots.

study_items.subject: Social Science
study_items.reason: Lower-priority selective breadth item included so the chapter is not fully untouched.
planning_notes: Keep this shortest and easiest to cut if time pressure rises.
Focus on soil types, resource classification, and one map pass.
Do not over-read the textbook here.
